2027-01-09.title: Saturday after Denho
readings: Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God?
You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition
2027-01-09.verse: You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.
theo: The Pharisees notice that some of Jesus' disciples eat with unwashed hands, against “the tradition of the elders”. Jesus answers with Isaiah: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” He does not despise tradition; the Church lives by Holy Tradition. He rejects the human customs that take the place of God's commandment and leave the heart untouched. The washing that matters is of the heart.

Paul faces a related question: if Israel was unfaithful, has God failed? “By no means! Although everyone is a liar, let God be proved true.” Our unfaithfulness does not cancel God's faithfulness. A few days after Denho, the feast of the Lord's baptism, we remember the washing God gave us in Baptism: not of hands but of hearts. Let our customs, fasts and devotions serve the love of God, not replace it.
outline: Ask: which of our customs help us love God, and which have become empty?
Our sin does not cancel his truth.
live: Look at one religious habit: is it still prayer from the heart?
Recall one time God was faithful when you were not.
2027-01-09.prayer: Faithful God, even when we are unfaithful, you remain true. Wash our hearts as you washed us in Baptism, and let all our customs and devotions spring from love for you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Before the anaphora the priest washes his hands and prays for purity of heart. The outward sign asks for the inward gift.

quick: Our unfaithfulness does not cancel God's faithfulness.
Human customs must not replace God's commandment.
The washing that matters is of the heart.
2027-01-09.action: Examine one religious habit: is it still prayer from the heart?
2027-01-09.question: Do I honour God only with my lips in some part of my life?

family.explain: Some leaders complained that Jesus' friends did not wash their hands in the right way. Jesus said: God wants your heart to be clean, not only your hands!
family.intention: We pray that our hearts may be clean and loving.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we keep our hearts clean?”

illus: A grandmother in Thiruvalla prayed the evening prayers every day for sixty years. One day her grandson asked why she sometimes stopped in the middle. She said: when I notice I am only saying words, I stop and tell God I love him, then I continue. Tradition with a heart.

pm.open: Faithful God, you are true even when we fail. Wash our hearts as we gather. Amen.
share: Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? (Romans 3:3). When has God been faithful to me?
This people honors me with their lips (Mark 7:6). Where are my lips and heart apart?
You abandon the commandment of God (Mark 7:8). Which custom of mine needs renewal?
pm.resp: Lord, create in us a clean heart.
interc: For the Church, that her traditions may always lead to the living God.
For those who feel their prayer has become empty.
For leaders, that they may not burden people with human rules.
For those who doubt God's faithfulness.
For our group, that our devotion may come from the heart.
pm.close: Faithful Father, you washed us in Baptism and remain true to your promises. Renew our hearts, so that all we do may honour you in truth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the Pharisees and scribes see Jesus' disciples eating with unwashed hands, against the tradition of the elders. They complain. Jesus answers with Isaiah: this people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Mark 7:6).

Jesus is not against tradition. Our Church lives by Holy Tradition, received from the Apostles. He is against human customs that replace God's commandment: you abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition (Mark 7:8).
St Paul asks: if some were unfaithful, will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? By no means! Let God be proved true (Romans 3:3–4). God's faithfulness is stronger than our failures.

A few days ago we celebrated Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. In our Baptism God washed not our hands but our hearts. Let us check our customs and devotions: do they come from the heart? Do they lead us to love God and neighbour? Then they are holy. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said God cares most about a clean heart. Washing hands is good, but a kind and loving heart is even better!

intro: God's faithfulness, God's commandment, and the washing of the heart.

sub: His mercies are new each morning.
q: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
What if some were unfaithful? Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God?
points.apply: Thank God for one sign of his faithfulness.

q: The Lord said: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their worship of me is a human commandment learned by rote;
You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.
points.apply: Renew one devotion so that it comes from the heart.

q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

concl: God is faithful even when we are not.
Let our traditions be the clothing of a loving heart.
2027-01-09.resolve: Go to Qurbono tomorrow with a renewed heart.
